warnings: Temporal pooling before the InfoNCE objective is now an explicit modeling assumption that discards temporal information and may reduce discriminative power for EEG representations, but this is no longer a correctness issue.
prepare_eeg_data() resets the global random number generator with torch.manual_seed(42), which can unintentionally affect reproducibility elsewhere if this function is reused.
The dataset is entirely synthetic and lacks realistic EEG preprocessing, subject metadata, and variability, making it appropriate only for validation or toy experiments.
The LOSO split is hard-coded to use the fifth subject as the test subject rather than providing a general LOSO iterator over all subjects.
suggested_fixes: Avoid resetting the global RNG inside reusable data-loading functions; accept a generator or seed externally if deterministic behavior is required.
Generalize the subject split so each subject can serve as the held-out test subject in a complete LOSO evaluation.
Document that temporal mean pooling is an intentional design choice and evaluate alternatives if temporal structure is expected to be informative.
Use realistic EEG datasets with subject metadata when validating research pipelines beyond unit tests.
summary: The previous blocking issues have been resolved. The data preparation now performs a subject-level split rather than a random train/test split, eliminating the previously identified subject leakage. The contrastive loss no longer contains the invalid reduction that caused a runtime error and now constructs a pairwise similarity matrix with a symmetric InfoNCE-style objective. No blocking regressions were introduced. The remaining concerns are non-blocking design and methodology warnings.
